name: Chain of Evidences / Evidence to Generate (CoE / E2G)
executive_summary: Instead of letting the model produce unverified reasoning claims, first extract only the thought sequences explicitly grounded in the given context as 'evidence,' then have the evidence itself drive output generation.
description: Targets a specific weakness shared by CoT, Self-Consistency, ReAct, Reflexion, and Tree of Thoughts: limited grounding in the actual provided context, leading to hallucinated or inconsistent claims, plus iterative sluggishness in the multi-step variants. CoE/E2G is a mono/dual-step zero-shot framework: it first identifies and extracts only the reasoning steps that are explicitly supported by the given context (the 'chain of evidences'), then uses that verified evidence — rather than free-generated reasoning — to guide the final output. Reports state-of-the-art results on knowledge-intensive reasoning and generation tasks, framed as faster and more reliable than the iterative multi-call methods it's compared against.
when_to_use: Knowledge-intensive, context-grounded reasoning tasks (retrieval-augmented QA, document-grounded generation) where hallucinated intermediate claims are a specific risk to avoid.
when_not_to_use: Tasks with no given context to ground evidence extraction against — the technique specifically depends on there being a source context to extract evidence from.
known_pitfalls: Evidence-extraction quality is a single point of failure: if genuinely relevant evidence is missed during extraction, the final generation is grounded in an incomplete evidence set.

primary_source.title: Chain of Evidences and Evidence to Generate: Prompting for Context Grounded and Retrieval Augmented Reasoning

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: A single LLM call (or a fixed sequence of them) with no external system dependency; running this template again at temperature 0 against the same model version should reproduce the same output.
